title: The Pleasures of Life
author: Sir John Lubbock
public_title: Why Less Work Boosts Joy Part 2 🤔
hook: You spend most of your waking hours at a desk.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You spend most of your waking hours at a desk. Centuries ago thinkers said true pleasure comes from less work. In 2019 the OECD measured average work weeks at about 40 hours. The result? Longer hours linked to lower life‑satisfaction scores. In 2020 the U.S. BLS reported Americans spend about 7.5 hours daily on work. They also track household chores in that same time. That's it. So why do we still glorify endless hustle? Because cultural myths, not data, drive our habits. What did Sir John Lubbock argue? He wrote that leisure should be the cornerstone of a good life. A 2022 Swedish trial found a six‑hour work week improved sleep and cut stress. That matches Lubbock’s call for balanced pleasure. So next time you log another overtime hour, remember the ancient advice and modern proof. You spend most of your waking hours at a desk.
